title: Garlic Butter Steak Skillet
subtitle: Melted provolone, peppers, one pan
description: Melted provolone, peppers, one pan. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Garlic Butter Steak Skillet in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use Bell peppers, sliced, Yellow onion, sliced as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Slice beef paper-thin
steps.instruction: Partially freeze ribeye 20 minutes; slice as thin as possible against the grain. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Sear beef and peppers
steps.instruction: Hot cast iron: sear beef in batches with onions and peppers until edges char. Season with salt and pepper. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground on an instant-read thermometer. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Melt provolone
steps.instruction: Pile beef mixture; lay provolone over top. Cover 1 minute until cheese melts into the meat. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Garlic Butter Steak Skillet onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Fill hoagies
steps.instruction: Scoop into toasted hoagie rolls. Philly Cheesesteak Skillet should drip a little — that's the point. Target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Philly Cheesesteak Skillet with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Philly Cheesesteak Skillet on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Melted provolone, peppers, one pan. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — Garlic Butter Steak Skillet runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
